questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was mostly the circumstances that made me apply for exchange in Bergen, but I'm very happy that it worked out that way. I can only recommend going to Bergen and Norway in general. The nature is incredible and just right in front of you. Bergen is surrounded by 7 mountains so its very easy and convenient to go hiking, running or biking. Looking back I would chose Bergen because of the nature and the vibe of the city. It's a smaller city but it's a student city and you really feel that from the very beginning, there is always a lot of life on the streets and in the cafes, bars and at the uni.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Going on exchange is the best semester on my bachelor, I've learned a lot both on an academical level and on a personal level

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was rather easy as we had an introduction day on the faculty. However, still a bit confusing as there is a lot of new platformes and informations.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a intro week with both more practical but also a lot of more social events. It was a very good way to get to know a bunch of people and the city from the very beginning. How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is very easy to find off campus housing in Bergen, and in other bigger cities in Norway due to the organisation called Sammen. Sammen offers a lot of different student housing within a very affordable range. I lived at Fantoft which I cna highly recommed as an exchange student. It is super easy to socialize with erasmus students aswell as Norwegians.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
You cant live on campus when going on UiB, and it is quite easy to find housing either through Sammen or by yourself fx on
Finn.no

questions.answer: It was very similar, lectures and seminars which is the same as SAU or classroom teaching.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go out of Bergen to explore the rest of Norway aswell. It is an amazing country and the nature is crazy. 
I can highly recommend to go to Lofoten and spent a week exploring the area. 
Also take the bus somewhere and go an a two or three day hike, it's the best memories and times with your new friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Denmark and Norway is quite similar, so pretty easy :))

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the organizations and student clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The alcohol prices. And the prices in general

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature is incredible and it's so easy to acces. That is for sure my favorite thing about Bergen.

questions.answer:
Explore the nature both in Bergen and outside of Bergen 
Just buy the stuff you want and do the stuff you want
Live at Fantoft

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: bring a sleeping bag, mat and hiking boots!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Everyday was a reward :)) 
I cant choose there was so many amazing experiences

questions.answer: To move to a new place without knowing anyone, but just after a few days or a week you feel at home
